questions.q: What is the difference between a functional and a non-functional requirement?
options: A functional requirement describes what the system does; a non-functional requirement describes how well it has to do it
Non-functional requirements describe features, functional requirements describe speed
Functional requirements only apply to batch systems, non-functional only to streaming
They are two names for the exact same concept
questions.explain: Both are necessary — a system that does the right thing slowly, or the wrong thing quickly, both fail the actual goal.

questions.q: Why is jumping straight to "I'll use an Eventstream and a KQL Database" risky without gathering requirements first?
options: This is always the correct first step regardless of requirements
Eventstreams and KQL Databases can never actually meet any real business requirement
It risks over-building, since Fabric's real-time machinery (like hopping windows) only matters once you know the actual freshness requirement
Non-functional requirements are irrelevant to tool selection
questions.explain: A city regulator's monthly report and a live dispatcher dashboard have very different actual requirements, driving very different correct designs.

questions.q: Which of these is a non-functional requirement, according to this lesson?
options: "Display a map of pickup locations"
"The dashboard must update within 5 minutes of a trip completing, and stay available 99.9% of the time"
"Show trip counts and average fare per vendor, per hour"
"Allow filtering by vendor ID"
questions.explain: This describes how well the system performs — speed and reliability — not what feature it provides.

questions.q: How does requirements gathering connect to Fabric Lesson 56's SLAs and SLOs?
options: They are completely unrelated concepts from different courses
Requirements gathering is where the number behind an SLO actually comes from — an SLO is meaningless without a real requirement driving it
SLAs and SLOs replace the need for requirements gathering entirely
Requirements gathering only applies after an SLO has already been set
questions.explain: A real requirement is also meaningless until it's been made concrete enough to turn into an actual measurable SLO.

questions.q: What kind of functional question should be asked before designing a system for "analyzing NYC taxi trips"?
options: What programming language should be used to write the code?
What color scheme should the dashboard use?
Analyze for whom, and what decisions does this data actually drive?
How many engineers are available on the team?
questions.explain: Different audiences (a dispatcher vs. a city regulator) lead to genuinely different correct designs.
